question: How do I open the Setup Dashboard?
answer: From the Setup Dashboard tile in Hub, with your normal Hub sign-in. If you see 'not switched on for your account', ask DFRNT to enable the tile for you.

question: Do I have to do the setup steps in order?
answer: Go in order the first time. Rates need vehicle sizes and zones, schedules need depots and customers, and partners need at least one customer to exist. You can revisit any step later.

question: What does 'Needs:' on a row mean?
answer: The row is missing a required field and was held back when you sent. The list after 'Needs:' names each missing item. Fill them in and press Save & send again; rows already created are not resent.

question: Why can't I mark a step as done?
answer: A step can be marked done only when it has no open requests to the tenant, every row is Created, and every required checklist item is ticked. The message under the button says which one is blocking.

question: What does 'Waiting on tenant' mean?
answer: DFRNT has asked the tenant for something on that step (for example a customer list) and it hasn't been marked Supplied yet. The header shows how many items are outstanding.

question: What is the difference between Save and Save & send?
answer: Save keeps your edits in the setup and nothing leaves the dashboard. Save & send also creates every complete row in Settings or Routed Operations as you, and shows the result per row.

question: If I send a step twice will it create duplicates?
answer: No. Sending again only sends rows that are not yet Created. Fix a held or failed row and resend; the others are skipped.

question: Why does it say my sign-in has expired?
answer: The dashboard acts in Settings and Routed Operations with your Hub sign-in. Sign in to Hub again in the same browser, then press Save & send again.

question: Will adding a customer email them?
answer: Yes. Settings always emails the primary contact a booking sign-in when a customer is created. That is why the row needs the 'send sign-in invite' tick before it is sent, and why nothing is sent until DFRNT has confirmed the tenant's email wording.

question: Does creating a courier send them an email?
answer: No. A courier gets a driver-app login with the password you typed; no email is sent. Give them the password yourself.

question: Why does every invite say waiting for DFRNT to confirm the system settings?
answer: Invites use the tenant's own sender address and wording, and a new database can carry another company's. DFRNT checks those settings and ticks the item on the Business step; invites then send on your next Save & send.

question: What are the DFRNT checklist items on the Business step?
answer: The tenant's own client file exists, the system settings and email wording are the tenant's, and depots are created. All three are required. Logo upload is optional.

question: What roles should I create first?
answer: An admin role and an operations role. Tick the Hub tiles each can open, then add people to them. People are emailed a Hub invite when sent, once the invite box is ticked.

question: Why does a person show 'Needs: a role called X on this step'?
answer: Their role must be one of the roles on the Team step. Add the role, or change the person's role to one that exists.

question: What does a customer need before it can be created?
answer: Client code, name, street address, suburb and city (US: city and state), invoice schedule, payment term, a primary contact with first name and email, and the invite tick. Everything else is optional.

question: Does the dashboard geocode customer addresses?
answer: No. Latitude and longitude are optional and not looked up. A customer created without them gets a note to set its map position in Settings before it is used on a client-address schedule.

question: My customer file has City and State but the step asks for Suburb and City. Which goes where?
answer: They are the same two fields. In a US tenant they are labelled City and State; elsewhere Suburb and City. Map City to the first and State to the second.

question: Can I set the invoice schedule for all customers at once?
answer: Yes. 'Invoice schedule for all' and 'Payment term for all' at the top of the Customers step set the value on every row. Adjust exceptions by hand.

question: How do I add more than one booking contact to a customer?
answer: Add them under the customer as other booking contacts, or import a contacts file keyed by client code after the customers are saved. Each gets a sign-in only if you tick 'Sign-in + invite'.

question: In what order are rates and zones created?
answer: Vehicle sizes, then zone groups, zones and zips, then fuel surcharges, then zone-to-zone rates, then distance rates. Enter them in any order; Save & send creates them in that sequence.

question: Can I create a speed or service on the Rates step?
answer: No. Speeds are picked from the tenant's existing list; the dashboard can't create one. Ask DFRNT (it is a checklist item on the step).

question: Why does my rate say 'Applies to every customer'?
answer: Its customer codes are blank. In Settings a rate with no customer list is a default rate for everyone. List client codes on the row to restrict it; those customers must have been created on the Customers step.

question: Is the driver rate required on a zone rate?
answer: Yes, Settings requires it. Enter 0 if drivers are paid another way.

question: Does a zone rate work in both directions?
answer: No. A to B and B to A are two rows. The dashboard does not mirror rates.

question: How do I enter a 12.5% fuel surcharge?
answer: Type 12.5 in Fuel % and give it a start date. The dashboard converts it for Settings. Leave the customer code blank for a general surcharge.

question: How do I load a lot of zips into zones?
answer: Use Import zips on the Rates step with a file of one row per zip: Zone Group, Zone Name, Zip / Post Code. Zones and groups are built from the names in the file.

question: What does a schedule need?
answer: A name, a destination depot, an origin type (depot, client address or direct) and at least one day window with start and end times. Depot origin also needs a pickup depot; client-address origin needs an origin depot and at least one customer.

question: Why are the depot pickers empty on the Schedules step?
answer: DFRNT hasn't created depots for this tenant yet. It is a required checklist item on the Business step.

question: Why does every courier need a password?
answer: Creating a courier creates their driver-app login, and Settings requires an initial password of 8 or more characters. You type it; it is sent once and never shown again.

question: Why isn't my courier in the fleet I picked?
answer: Creating a courier can't set the fleet. Assign couriers to fleets in Settings > Driver List after sending; the row's note says which fleet you chose.

question: Why did my first partner fail on a new tenant?
answer: Settings copies site and billing values for a new partner from an existing customer. Create one customer first, then send the partner again.

question: Where do I set up notifications and auto-assign rules?
answer: In Settings > Automations, linked from the Automations step. Rules go live as soon as they are saved there, so set them up after rates and schedules. Tick the item on the step when done.

question: Where do I connect Xero, carriers or Shopify?
answer: In Integration Manager, linked from the Integrations step. The dashboard tracks it as a checklist item you tick when each connection is made.

question: What are the training levels?
answer: Rookie from 0 XP, Operator from 100, Pro from 300, Expert from 600 and Master from 1000. Each role's Master challenge unlocks when all its other challenges are done.

question: Does importing a file create records in Settings?
answer: No. Loading a file only fills the step's rows. Records are created when you press Save & send on the step.

question: What file types does Smart Import accept?
answer: CSV, XLSX and XLS with a header row, one record per row. Excel files are read from the first sheet with data.

question: What does the confidence percentage mean on the mapping screen?
answer: How closely your column name matched a dashboard field: green 80% and above, amber 50 to 79, red below. Matches under 75% are left for you to pick, or shown as "AI suggestion - check it" when AI suggestions are on. You can change any mapping.

question: Which old systems does Smart Import recognise?
answer: Key Software, Elite EXTRA, Datatrac, OnTime, GetSwift, Track-POD and DFRNT exports, by their column names. Recognition only labels the file; any CSV or Excel file with a header row can be mapped.

question: Can I import my job history?
answer: No. The setup loads customers, contacts, drivers, zones, zone rates and team members only. Export master lists from your old system, not job lists.

question: What columns does a customer file need?
answer: Required: Client Code, Client Name, Street Address, Suburb (US: City), City (US: State), Primary Contact First Name, Primary Contact Email. Optional: unit, post or zip code, country, phone, company email, invoice email, contact surname and mobile.

question: How does a contacts file say which customer a contact belongs to?
answer: By Client Code (the customer's exact name also works). Import and save the customers first; a contact whose code matches no customer on the step is skipped.

question: Can I put driver passwords in the import file?
answer: No. Passwords are never read from a file. After import each courier shows 'Needs: initial app password' until you type one on the step.

question: What does a zones file look like?
answer: Three columns, one row per zip: Zone Group, Zone Name, Zip / Post Code. Rows sharing a zone name are gathered into that zone.

question: Why isn't speed in the rates file?
answer: Old systems name services in their own words, so the file carries zones, charges and vehicle size only. Pick the speed on each row after import.

question: My rates are a matrix of zones. How do I import it?
answer: Unpivot it to one row per cell: Rate Name, From Zone, To Zone, Customer Charge, Driver Rate, Vehicle Size. A spreadsheet pivot or a short script does it.

question: What does a team file need?
answer: First Name, Email and Role for each person; last name, job title and mobile are optional. Role must match a role name on the Team step.

question: What exports do I need from my old system?
answer: Five: customers (accounts), customer contacts or users, drivers, your zone or zip table, and your rate table, each as CSV or Excel with a header row. Not job history.

question: Will Deliver Different log in to my old system to migrate my data?
answer: No. You export the files and upload them. Anything the files lack is filled in on the step before it is sent.

question: What does 'already taken' mean while I'm typing?
answer: The code, name or email already exists for this tenant, including on inactive records. Choose another. 'Unchecked' means the check couldn't run; the owning app still enforces uniqueness on send.

question: Why does a row say 'Needs: customer X created on the Clients step'?
answer: A rate, surcharge or schedule names a customer code the dashboard didn't create. Add and send that customer first, or clear the codes so the item applies to every customer.

question: What has to exist before I start on an empty tenant?
answer: DFRNT confirms the system settings and email wording, creates the tenant's own client file and depots, and makes sure speeds exist. Then do Team, one customer, vehicle sizes and zones, rates, schedules, fleets and couriers, partners last.

question: How long is my setup kept?
answer: 120 days from the last change. It reopens on the browser you used; others from the same tenant can open it too. Unsaved edits on the current step are not kept, so Save before closing.

question: If I delete a setup are the records it created removed?
answer: No. Records created in Settings or Routed Operations stay. Deleting a setup only removes the dashboard's session.

question: Why doesn't the dashboard fill in defaults for missing fields?
answer: An earlier tool did, and sample values ended up on real customer records. Now a missing required field holds the row back with 'Needs:' so nothing invented reaches Settings.
